system_description.narrative_title: US–China techno-economic rivalry ahead of Xi-Trump summit
system_description.narrative_summary: The single dominant narrative is an intensifying US–China techno-economic competition centered on semiconductors, AI hardware, memory, rare earths and electric vehicles, amplified by the diplomatic context of Xi Jinping's US visit. Headlines show Chinese firms scaling up chip and memory production while US officials, allies and industries weigh export controls, market access restrictions and investment shifts; simultaneous talks and meetings aim to manage supply-chain and strategic-material risks. The net effect is active reconfiguration of supply chains, investment destinations (India, Mexico, Japan, EU responses) and regulatory levers as both sides jockey for technological advantage and economic security.
system_description.scope: Actors, flows and policy levers shaping technology and strategic supply chains between the US and China during the summit window: semiconductor and memory production and investment; AI chip demand; critical minerals/rare-earth transactions; automotive/EV market access and trade measures; corporate lobbying; export controls, licensing, tariffs and summit-level diplomacy.
system_description.super_system: Global economic-security order (trade regimes, alliances and great-power strategic competition)
adjacent_subsystems: Semiconductor and AI hardware supply chain

variables.name: Semiconductor fabrication capacity
variables.description: Aggregate installed and operable advanced semiconductor fabrication capacity measured in wafer starts or equivalent production throughput.

variables.name: Memory chip fabrication capacity
variables.description: Total production capacity dedicated to memory (NAND/DRAM) manufacturing measured in wafers or gigabytes-equivalent output.

variables.name: AI hardware demand rate
variables.description: Rate of demand growth for specialized AI accelerators and related hardware measured as change in procurement or shipments per unit time.

variables.name: Critical materials supply concentration
variables.description: Degree to which extraction, processing and export of critical minerals and rare-earth elements are concentrated among limited suppliers or regions.

variables.name: Supply-chain geographic diversity
variables.description: Distributional spread of key suppliers and production nodes across different countries or regions, indicating diversification level.

variables.name: Cross-border investment flows
variables.description: Volume and direction of investment flows (FDI, greenfield, mergers) between economic blocs and alternative destinations per unit time.

variables.name: Technology transfer and licensing rate
variables.description: Rate at which advanced know-how, patents and licensing agreements move across borders or between firms measured per period.

variables.name: Export control strictness
variables.description: Degree of legal and administrative restrictiveness applied to outbound transfer of specified technologies, components and tooling.

variables.name: Market access barrier level
variables.description: Intensity of tariffs, licensing conditions, quotas and administrative hurdles that limit foreign firms' access to a given market.

variables.name: Regulatory cooperation and alignment
variables.description: Degree of harmonization or formal cooperation in regulatory standards and licensing regimes between relevant jurisdictions.

variables.name: Corporate lobbying pressure
variables.description: Intensity of private-sector advocacy efforts aimed at shaping trade, investment and technology policy outcomes measured by activity and influence.

variables.name: Strategic stockpiles of critical inputs
variables.description: Quantities of reserve inventories of critical minerals, components or finished tech products held for strategic or security purposes.

variables.name: Fabrication construction and capital cost
variables.description: Realized and expected capital expenditure per unit capacity for building semiconductor and memory production facilities.

variables.name: Supply-chain resilience
variables.description: System-level ability of technology supply chains to absorb, adapt to and recover from shocks measured by recovery time and redundancy.

variables.name: Perceived geopolitical risk
variables.description: Market and policymaker perception of geopolitical tension and conflict risk that influences strategic decisions and risk premia.

variables.name: Alternative destination attractiveness
variables.description: Relative attractiveness of non-primary locations for investment and production based on cost, policy incentives and supply-chain fit.
